issues.passage: He preferred the tortuous staircase that climbed in one unbroken flight to the landing.
issues.why: A winding or spiral staircase is both tortuous (full of twists) and often one unbroken flight (no intermediate landing). The passage is natural, correct use of tortuous = full of twists; a student who knows the word would accept it.

fix.correctPassage: Negotiators spent months on a tortuous route through conflicting statutes before reaching a draft.
wrongPassages: The highway ran in a tortuous straight line across the plain with no curves for miles.
Her tortuous brief reduced the entire dispute to three plain sentences anyone could follow.
He preferred the tortuous staircase that rose in a single straight run with no turns to the landing.
